name: request_routing
description: Parses a raw user request string into a structured CapabilityDemand — an ordered list of capabilities required to satisfy the request. Single entry point into the AIOS execution pipeline. Per Constitution Principle 1 (Capability-First), the kernel does 90% routing, 10% generation.

inputs.name: request_text
inputs.description: Raw natural-language request from the operator or CLI.

inputs.name: session_context
inputs.description: Active session metadata: project root, active brain, loaded packs. Empty when no session.

outputs.name: demand
outputs.description: CapabilityDemand { request_id: AIOS-REQ-NNNNNN, capabilities: AIOS-CAPABILITY-NNNNNN[], intent: string, constraints: object }

outputs.name: confidence
outputs.description: Routing confidence 0.0-1.0. Below 0.6 triggers a clarification request per Engineering Law 12.

side_effects: Allocates a new AIOS-REQ-NNNNNN request id

error_codes.message: Request text is empty or whitespace only.
error_codes.recovery: Prompt operator for a non-empty request.

error_codes.message: No installed capability matches the request intent.
error_codes.recovery: Emit clarification request (Engineering Law 12) listing candidate capabilities and required packs.

error_codes.message: Multiple capabilities match with confidence gap < 0.15.
error_codes.recovery: Present ranked candidates; default to the highest-confidence unless operator disambiguates.

examples: { request_text: 'build a user-auth feature with email + oauth' } -> demand.capabilities = [goal_decomposition, project_understanding, code_generation, unit_testing, code_review]
